the inhomogeneous and homogeneous static magnetic fields combined to γ radiation did not influence the repair of γ irradiation‐damaged DNA in leukocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of static magnetic fields (SME) combined with gamma radiation, on the repair of radiation damaged DNA on human leukocytes.
the effects of inhomogeneous and homogeneous static magnetic field on radiation‐damaged leukocyte DNA.
the effects of static magnetic fields (magnetic flux density of 0.3 to 159.2 mT) on the DNA damage and repair.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the exposure to SMFs before and after 60Co‐gamma irradiation has no effect on the DNA damage, while exposure to SMFs following 60Co‐ gamma irradiation has a positive effect on DNA repair.
the SMF exposure has a minor effect on DNA repair, but it can be observed that the effect is time‐ and dose‐dependent.
inhomogeneous static fields (SMFs), with a gradient of 47, 1.3, or 0, 3 T/m, and a periodicity of 10 mm, do not have any significant effect on the repair of radiation induced DNA damage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the exposure of cells to static magnetic fields (both homogeneous and inhomogeneously) before and after gamma‐irradiation has no significant effect on DNA damage.
the exposure to SMF has no effect on the radiation damage to DNA and DNA repair in leukocytes.
SMF exposure following 4 GY gamma irradiation does not affect the DNA repair.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SMFs do not have any effect on DNA damage or repair.
inhomogeneous SMF has a protective effect on radiation‐induced DNA damage.
inhomogeneous static SMFs with a gradient of 47 T/m can influence the repair of gamma‐irradiation damaged DNA on human lymphocytes.
